yer.title: The Placebo Effect
ss: The placebo effect refers to a real improvement in a patient's condition that follows a treatment with no active ingredient.
For decades, doctors regarded it as a nuisance that made it harder to test new drugs.
However, researchers have increasingly come to see it as a valuable phenomenon in its own right.
In one well-known study, patients who received sugar pills reported significantly less pain than those who received no treatment at all.
Such findings suggest that expectations alone can trigger measurable changes in the body.
Even so, critics warn that the effect is often exaggerated, since many patients would have recovered naturally.
yer.why: Eksik cümle bir çalışmayı anlatıyor ('In one well-known study'). Hemen ardından gelen 'Such findings' bu çalışmanın bulgularına gönderme yapıyor; bu yüzden cümle 'Such findings…' cümlesinden hemen önce olmalı.

yer.title: Filter Bubbles
ss: Online platforms rarely show every user the same information.
Instead, algorithms select content that is likely to keep each individual scrolling.
As a result, users are gradually surrounded by opinions that confirm what they already believe.
The writer Eli Pariser called this invisible environment a 'filter bubble'.
Some researchers, nevertheless, argue that the danger has been overstated.
They point out that most people still encounter opposing views, if only through arguments with friends and relatives.
yer.why: 'As a result' bir sonuç bildirir. Nedeni bir önceki cümlede: algoritmalar kullanıcıyı ekranda tutacak içeriği seçiyor. Sonrasında gelen 'this invisible environment' de bu cümlede anlatılan ortama gönderme yapıyor.

yer.title: The Coffee Houses of London
ss: In the late seventeenth century, coffee houses spread rapidly across London.
For the price of a single cup, any man could sit for hours, read newspapers and join the conversation.
Unlike taverns, these places were associated with sober and serious discussion.
It is therefore hardly surprising that they soon became centres of political debate and business.
Several famous institutions, including an insurance market, began as informal meetings in such rooms.
The government, worried about criticism, even tried to close them in 1675, but the attempt failed within days.
yer.why: 'Unlike taverns' bir karşılaştırma yapıyor ve kahvehanelerin ciddi tartışma yerleri olduğunu söylüyor. Sonraki cümledeki 'It is therefore hardly surprising' bu özelliğe dayanarak bir sonuç çıkarıyor; yani karşılaştırma cümlesi tam ondan önce gelmeli.

yer.title: The Testing Effect
ss: Most students prepare for exams by reading their notes again and again.
Psychologists, however, have found that this strategy is surprisingly inefficient.
Students who test themselves remember considerably more than those who simply reread the same material.
This phenomenon, known as the testing effect, appears to work because retrieving information strengthens the memory of it.
In other words, the act of remembering is not only a way of measuring learning but also a way of producing it.
Teachers who give frequent low-stakes quizzes may therefore help their students more than they realise.
yer.why: 'In other words' bir önceki cümleyi başka sözlerle yeniden söyler. Önceki cümle hatırlamanın belleği güçlendirdiğini anlatıyor; eksik cümle de hatırlamanın öğrenmeyi 'ürettiğini' söylüyor. Sonraki 'therefore' ise bu fikirden sonuç çıkarıyor.

yer.title: Realism in Documentary Film
ss: Documentary films are often treated as transparent windows onto reality.
Yet every documentary is the product of countless choices made by its director.
Deciding where to place the camera, which scenes to keep and what music to add all shape the viewer's understanding.
For example, the same interview can appear sympathetic or hostile depending on the shots placed before and after it.
Audiences who are aware of these choices are less likely to accept a film's message uncritically.
This does not mean that documentaries are lies; it means that they are interpretations.
yer.why: 'For example' bir önceki genel iddiayı örneklendirir. Önceki cümle yönetmenin seçimlerinin izleyicinin anlayışını biçimlendirdiğini söylüyor; röportaj örneği tam olarak bunu gösteriyor.

yer.title: Whistleblowing
ss: A whistleblower is an employee who reveals illegal or unethical practices within an organisation.
Many societies celebrate such individuals as heroes who protect the public interest.
Their colleagues, by contrast, frequently regard them as disloyal.
This tension explains why whistleblowers often pay a heavy personal price, from losing their jobs to being isolated by former friends.
To reduce these costs, several countries have introduced laws that protect employees who report wrongdoing.
Critics contend, though, that such laws are rarely enforced and that the fear of retaliation remains.
yer.why: 'By contrast' önceki cümleyle zıtlık kurar: toplum onları kahraman olarak görürken iş arkadaşları sadakatsiz görüyor. Sonraki 'This tension' de tam olarak bu iki görüş arasındaki gerilime gönderme yapıyor.

ana.title: Conformity
ana.p: When people are uncertain how to behave, they often look to others for guidance. In a series of experiments in the 1950s, Solomon Asch asked participants to judge the length of lines after hearing several confederates give obviously wrong answers. Around one third of the responses followed the incorrect majority. Interestingly, conformity dropped sharply when just one other person disagreed with the group. The experiments therefore suggest that social pressure is powerful but fragile: a single ally can be enough to resist it.

o.t: Toplumsal baskı güçlüdür ama kırılgandır; tek bir destekçi bile çoğunluğa direnmeyi sağlayabilir.
Asch'ın deneylerinde cevapların yaklaşık üçte biri yanlış çoğunluğu izledi.
İnsanlar emin olmadıklarında kararlarını her zaman çoğunluğa göre verir.
Deneylerde kullanılan yöntem, katılımcıları kandırdığı için etik açıdan sorunludur.

ana.title: Sugar and Industry
ana.p: In the second half of the twentieth century, food manufacturers discovered that sugar could solve a commercial problem. When fat was removed from products to make them appear healthier, they often lost their flavour. Adding sugar restored the taste at a low cost. As a consequence, sugar began to appear in foods where consumers would never expect it, from bread to soup. Some nutritionists argue that this hidden sugar, rather than personal weakness, largely explains why modern diets contain so much of it.

o.t: Yağı azaltılan ürünlerin tadını korumak için eklenen gizli şeker, modern diyetlerdeki yüksek şeker tüketiminin başlıca nedeni olabilir.
Yağı alınan ürünler çoğu zaman lezzetini kaybetti.
Şeker tüketimi tamamen tüketicilerin kişisel zayıflığından kaynaklanır.
Şeker, tarih boyunca yalnızca zenginlerin karşılayabildiği bir lükstü.

ana.title: Artificial Intelligence and Creativity
ana.p: Whether machines can be creative depends largely on how creativity is defined. If it simply means producing something new, then many programs already qualify, since they generate images and texts that have never existed before. Most researchers, however, insist that a creative work must also be valuable and that its maker must understand why it is valuable. By this stricter standard, current systems fall short: they recombine patterns from their training data without any sense of purpose. The debate, in short, is less about technology than about the meaning of the word itself.

o.t: Makinelerin yaratıcı olup olmadığı tartışması teknolojiden çok 'yaratıcılık' kavramının nasıl tanımlandığına bağlıdır.
Bazı programlar daha önce hiç var olmamış görüntü ve metinler üretebilir.
Araştırmacıların çoğuna göre bugünkü sistemler gerçek anlamda yaratıcıdır.
Bilgisayar bilimi, ilk olarak askeri amaçlarla geliştirilmiştir.

ana.title: Reading on Screens
ana.p: Studies comparing reading on paper and on screens have produced a surprisingly consistent result. For short or simple texts, the medium makes little difference. For long and complex texts, however, readers tend to understand less when they read on a screen, especially when they are under time pressure. Researchers suggest that the screen encourages a habit of skimming, in which the eye jumps from keyword to keyword. The problem, then, is not the device itself but the reading behaviour that people have learned to associate with it.

o.t: Ekranda okumadaki asıl sorun cihaz değil, ekranla ilişkilendirilen hızlı ve yüzeysel okuma alışkanlığıdır.
Kısa ve basit metinlerde okuma ortamı pek fark yaratmaz.
Ekranda okuyanlar her tür metni kâğıtta okuyanlardan daha az anlar.
Okul kütüphaneleri dijital kaynaklara daha fazla bütçe ayırmalıdır.

ana.title: Relative Deprivation
ana.p: It might seem logical that the poorest groups in a society would be the most likely to rebel. History, however, suggests otherwise. Revolutions have frequently broken out not when conditions were at their worst, but after a period of improvement that suddenly came to an end. Sociologists explain this pattern with the idea of relative deprivation: people compare their situation not with an absolute standard, but with what they have come to expect. When reality falls behind these rising expectations, frustration grows, even among those who are comparatively well off.

o.t: İsyanı, mutlak yoksulluktan çok beklentiler ile gerçek durum arasındaki farkın yarattığı hayal kırıklığı tetikler.
Devrimler çoğu zaman bir iyileşme döneminin ardından çıkmıştır.
Toplumdaki en yoksul gruplar her zaman ilk isyan edenlerdir.
Sosyal medya, toplumsal hareketlerin örgütlenmesini kolaylaştırır.

ana.title: Moral Luck
ana.p: We usually believe that people should be judged only for what they can control. Yet our everyday judgments often contradict this principle. Imagine two drivers who both fall asleep at the wheel; one wakes up in time, while the other hits a pedestrian. Although their behaviour was identical, we blame the second driver far more severely. Philosophers call this phenomenon moral luck, and it raises an uncomfortable question: if outcomes beyond our control shape how we are judged, how fair are our moral and legal systems?

o.t: Kontrol edemediğimiz sonuçlar insanları nasıl yargıladığımızı etkiler; bu da ahlaki ve hukuki sistemlerin adaletini sorgulatır.
Direksiyonda uyuyan iki sürücüden yalnızca biri yayaya çarpar.
İnsanları yalnızca kontrol edebildikleri şeylere göre yargılarız.
Uykusuzluk, trafik kazalarının en önemli nedenidir.
